extra.message: Insecure Deserialization via pickle.loads() on Untrusted Input — Remote code execution on the server; full system compromise. [verified: Same as finding [2]: pickle.loads() on untrusted input at line 65-73; arbitrary code execution.]

Arbitrary code execution via eval() in case_formula_cast_253 — Remote code execution — attacker can run arbitrary Python code on the server, gaining full system access. [verified: Same as finding [0]: eval(expr, ...) at line 78 on attacker GET param; sandbox escape via ().__class__.__mro__ chain.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via User Jinja2 Fragment — Remote code execution on the server; full system compromise. [verified: Same as finding [1]: Jinja2 Template injection from GET fragment at line 114-133; SSTI enables code execution.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Write via User-Supplied Filename — Arbitrary file write outside intended directory; potential overwrite of critical system or application files. [verified: Same as finding [5]: user-controlled filename in Path / join at line 119-142; arbitrary file write with mkdir and write_bytes.]

Server-Side Template Injection via user-controlled Jinja2 fragment — Remote code execution on the server. [verified: Same as finding [1]: Jinja2 Template constructed from user fragment at line 133; SSTI enables arbitrary code execution.]

NoSQL Injection via User-Controlled MongoDB Query — Arbitrary MongoDB query execution; data exfiltration, query logic bypass, potential code execution via $where. [verified: Same as finding [4]: raw MongoDB query from user JSON body at line 135-160; $where JavaScript execution and query bypass.]

Hardcoded default Django SECRET_KEY fallback — Complete compromise of session integrity, CSRF protection, and password reset tokens. [verified: Same hardcoded SECRET_KEY fallback on settings.py line 9-12; the known default key undermines all Django cryptographic signing, enabling session/CSRF/password-reset token forgery.]

Hardcoded default Django SECRET_KEY — Session forgery, CSRF token forgery, and password reset token forgery if the application is deployed without overriding the default SECRET_KEY via environment variable. [verified: Same hardcoded SECRET_KEY default on settings.py line 9-12; the known literal string makes all Django-signed tokens (session, CSRF, password-reset) forgeable.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints — Unrestricted credential brute-forcing; account takeover via password guessing. [verified: Same finding as idx 0: LoginView at /accounts/login/ (accounts/urls.py:7) lacks any rate limiting — no throttling library, no custom middleware, no login attempt tracking. Credential brute-forcing is unmitigated.]

Missing Authorization — Any Attorney Can Edit Any Client's PII (IDOR) — A malicious attorney can view and modify any client's sensitive PII, change client status to sabotage representation, and reassign portal user accounts to hijack client access — all without being assigned to that client's matters. [verified: client_edit only gates on FIRM_ADMIN/ATTORNEY role but omits the matter-ownership check that client_detail and client_list enforce via matters_visible_to().filter(client=client).exists(); access.py has no can_edit_client, and no middleware compensates, so any attorney can modify any client's PII, status, and portal_user by guessing client_id.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via copyline Parameter — Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser; session theft, credential harvesting, page manipulation. [verified: Same as finding [6]: copyline GET param in unescaped HTML at line 29-32; reflected XSS.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped copyline parameter in HTML response — Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session. [verified: Same as finding [6]: copyline concatenated into unescaped HTML response at line 32; reflected XSS.]

Sensitive data (Authorization header) logged in cleartext in case_wire_tally_212 — Bearer tokens and sensitive credentials written to application logs; log injection allows attackers to forge audit trails or inject malicious log entries that mislead investigations. [verified: Same as finding [8]: logger.warning at line 72 logs Authorization header and full body; credential leakage to logs.]

Sensitive data (bearer tokens/request body) logged at WARNING level in /ops/wire/case-tally-212/ — Exposure of authentication credentials (API keys, internal ops tokens) and request data in log files, enabling credential theft and lateral movement. [verified: Same as finding [8]: logger.warning logs Authorization header and body at line 74; INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN leakage to logs.]

Sensitive data (Authorization header and request body) logged at WARNING level via /ops/ endpoint — Leakage of INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN and other secrets to logs, enabling lateral movement [verified: Same as finding [8]: logger.warning at line 80 logs Authorization header and full body; INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN and other secrets written to logs in plaintext.]

XXE via lxml Parser with DTD and External Entity Resolution Enabled — Local file disclosure, server-side request forgery, denial of service. [verified: Same as finding [3]: lxml parser with DTD and entity resolution at line 159-192; XXE file disclosure.]

XXE via lxml XML parser with DTD and entities enabled in /ops/xml/case-fold-455/ — Local file disclosure, SSRF, or denial of service via external entity processing in XML parser. [verified: Same as finding [3]: etree.fromstring with dangerous parser at line 183-192; XXE file disclosure via external entities.]

DEBUG mode enabled by default — Sensitive information disclosure — stack traces, settings including SECRET_KEY, database credentials, file paths, environment variables exposed to anyone triggering an error. [verified: settings.py line 13-14 defaults DEBUG to True via os.environ.get('DJANGO_DEBUG','true'), exposing full stack traces, settings, and env vars on any unhandled exception; no production override found.]

DEBUG mode enabled by default in settings.py — Detailed error pages with stack traces, settings, and local variables exposed to unauthenticated users — leading to information disclosure including database credentials, SECRET_KEY, and internal code structure. [verified: Same DEBUG=True default on settings.py line 13-14; Django's debug error pages expose SECRET_KEY, DB credentials, and internal code structure to unauthenticated requesters.]

Session cookies missing Secure flag when DEBUG is True (default) — Session cookies transmitted over HTTP can be intercepted via man-in-the-middle attacks — session hijacking. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = not DEBUG evaluates to False when DEBUG=True (the default), so session cookies lack the Secure flag and can be sent over unencrypted HTTP.]

Session Cookies Transmitted Without Secure Flag When DEBUG=True — Session hijacking via network sniffing when the application runs with DEBUG=True over HTTP. [verified: Same SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = not DEBUG; with DEBUG=True (default), session cookies lack Secure, enabling session theft via network sniffing on HTTP connections.]

Insecure cookie flags and missing HSTS when DEBUG=True (the default) — Session cookies transmitted over unencrypted HTTP are vulnerable to network sniffing and session hijacking. Missing HSTS allows SSL-stripping attacks. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE both evaluate to False under default DEBUG=True, and SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS is never set, leaving session/CSRF cookies transmittable over HTTP and vulnerable to SSL-stripping.]

Account enumeration via disabled-account error message on login — An attacker can enumerate valid usernames and determine which accounts are disabled, facilitating targeted attacks and social engineering. [verified: The /accounts/login/ endpoint is unauthenticated with no rate limiting. 'This account is disabled.' (valid credentials + disabled account) is distinct from the generic invalid-credentials error, revealing both username existence and password correctness for disabled accounts.]

Open Redirect via next parameter in notification_read — An attacker can redirect authenticated users to arbitrary external websites, enabling credential phishing or malware delivery by crafting a link or form that POSTs to this endpoint with a malicious next URL. [verified: Line 79 passes request.POST.get('next') directly to Django redirect() with zero URL validation — no url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme() or is_safe_url() check exists anywhere in the codebase, and CSRF enforcement (require_POST) validates request origin but does not constrain the redirect target.]

CSV Formula Injection in Export Functions — Arbitrary command execution on the spreadsheet user's machine when the exported CSV is opened; data exfiltration via DDE/CSV injection. [verified: The three CSV export functions at line 231+ write matter titles, client names, document tags, and attorney usernames to csv.writer.writerow() without any sanitization for formula-trigger characters; DocumentForm.clean_tags() only checks isprintable() which passes =+−@, and MatterForm/ClientForm lack any title/name sanitization.]

CSV formula injection in spreadsheet exports — Arbitrary command execution on the system of any user who opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application, enabling malware delivery or data exfiltration. [verified: At line 239, m.title is written unsanitized to CSV; both MatterForm (no clean_title) and DocumentForm (no title sanitization) allow formula characters through. The _csv_response helper returns a bare csv.writer with no cell-escaping wrapper, and no middleware or decorator intercepts the CSV output to prefix dangerous cells.]

CSV formula injection in matter/deadline/document CSV exports — When exported CSV files are opened in spreadsheet applications, attacker-crafted document tags/titles/references execute arbitrary commands via DDE or formula injection, potentially leading to code execution on the victim's machine. [verified: At line 312, d.tags is written directly to CSV; DocumentForm.clean_tags() filters only non-printable chars—=, +, −, and @ are printable and pass through. No downstream control in csv.writer or the _csv_response helper prefixes formula-trigger characters, so injected tags reach the CSV output unchanged.]

Non-Constant-Time Comparison of Internal Operations Token — An attacker may be able to determine the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN value via timing analysis, gaining access to all 19 dangerous /ops/ endpoints. [verified: Same as finding [24]: _wrk_gate uses == comparison at line 20; timing side-channel leaks token character-by-character.]

Cookie set without HttpOnly/Secure flags in /ops/crumb/case-lane-291/ — Cookie accessible to client-side JavaScript enabling theft via XSS, and transmissible over unencrypted HTTP connections enabling network interception. [verified: Same as finding [46]: set_cookie('portal_crumb', marker) at line 89 without Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags.]

Insecure Cookie Set Without Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite Flags — Cookie accessible via JavaScript (no HttpOnly), transmitted over HTTP (no Secure), vulnerable to cross-site requests (no SameSite). [verified: response.set_cookie('portal_crumb', marker) at line 90 lacks Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags; cookie value from user-controlled GET param enables client-side theft and MITM.]

Permissive CORS with Reflected Origin and Credentials — Cross-origin requests from any attacker-controlled domain can include credentials; session/token theft from authenticated users. [verified: Same as finding [7]: CORS mirrors Origin with credentials at lines 108-125.]

Permissive CORS with credential reflection in case_origin_mirror_374 — Any website can make authenticated cross-origin requests to this endpoint with the user's credentials, enabling CSRF-style attacks from any origin. [verified: Same as finding [7]: Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflects request Origin with credentials true at line 109-125.]

Permissive CORS with credential reflection from request origin — Cross-origin requests with credentials enabled from any origin. [verified: Same as finding [7]: permissive CORS with reflected origin and credentials true at lines 124-125.]

Use of Weak PRNG (random.choice) for Token Generation — Predictable token values; potential for token forgery or bypass of randomness-based security controls. [verified: Same as finding [11]: random.choice() for token generation at line 129-151; Mersenne Twister outputs predictable.]

Weak PRNG (random.choice) used for token generation in case_nonce_roll_404 — Attacker who observes enough generated codes can predict future tokens, leading to token forgery and authentication bypass. [verified: Same as finding [11]: random.choice(alphabet) at line 133-151 for code generation; Mersenne Twister outputs predictable.]

Weak PRNG (random.choice) for token generation in /ops/nonce/case-roll-404/ — Predictable tokens enabling session hijacking, CSRF bypass, or other attacks relying on token unpredictability. [verified: Same as finding [11]: random.choice(alphabet) at line 142-151; weak PRNG used for token generation.]

Disabled SSL/TLS Certificate Verification on Outbound Requests — Man-in-the-middle attack; interception and modification of data in transit to external services. [verified: Same as finding [28]: ssl._create_unverified_context() at line 148-176 disables TLS verification on outbound requests.]

SSRF with disabled TLS verification in case_trust_drift_434 — Man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound connections; if the endpoint URL were ever made dynamic, SSRF to internal services would succeed without certificate validation. [verified: Hardcoded URL prevents SSRF, but ssl._create_unverified_context() at line 155-176 disables TLS verification on outbound connection, enabling MITM.]

TLS certificate verification disabled in /ops/trust/case-drift-434/ — Man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound HTTPS connections, enabling data interception and manipulation. [verified: Same as finding [28]: ssl._create_unverified_context() at line 167-176 disables TLS certificate verification.]

Hardcoded Default Database Credentials in Settings — Database compromise if defaults are used in deployment or repository is exposed. [verified: settings.py line 78-79 hardcodes default DATABASE_USER='legal_firm' and DATABASE_PASSWORD='legal_firm' as fallbacks; committed credentials grant DB access if env vars are not overridden in deployment.]

Username enumeration via explicit error messages on registration — Attacker can enumerate valid usernames on the system — aids in credential stuffing and targeted password attacks. [verified: The invitation_accept view is unauthenticated and exposes 'Username is taken.' on repeated POST attempts without consuming the token. However, exploitation requires a valid 256-bit urandom invitation token (trusted per threat model, 72h expiry), so practical impact is minimal.]

User enumeration via differential responses on invitation accept endpoint — Attacker can probe for existence of invitation tokens and distinguish valid from invalid tokens [verified: Lines 252–258 return Http404 for non-existent tokens vs 410 for tokens that exist but are expired/revoked/accepted, with no rate-limiting or throttling found anywhere in the project; the 32-byte urlsafe tokens resist brute-force but the differential status code leaks whether invitations were ever created.]

Mass Assignment via Untrusted JSON Merge into Workspace Object — Privilege escalation; attacker can set is_admin=True or change role to gain administrative access. [verified: Request JSON body merged into local workset dict via update() at line 41 with no field whitelist; attacker can inject is_admin/role fields, though impact limited to this endpoint's response context.]

Sensitive PII (SSN-like tax_ref) exposed in case_matter_fold_018 response — Exposure of what appears to be a real SSN in API responses; may violate privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) and enable identity theft. [verified: Same as finding [9]: tax_ref '739-44-1982' at line 44 follows SSN format; synthetic PII-formatted data exposed.]

User-controlled cookie value set from GET parameter in case_crumb_lane_291 — Attacker can inject arbitrary cookie values, potentially enabling session fixation or other cookie-based attacks in conjunction with the mirrored XSS endpoint. [verified: GET param 'marker' flows to set_cookie and JSON response at line 85-89; Django sanitizes newlines in cookies so response splitting is mitigated, but user-controlled cookie value lacks security flags.]

Filesystem path disclosure in error messages in case_pulse_spill_346 — Attacker learns internal server directory structure, aiding further path traversal or file-based attacks. [verified: Same as finding [13]: RuntimeError f-string at line 91-103 exposes BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path to client.]

Filesystem Path Disclosure via Error Message Reflection — Reconnaissance; attacker learns internal server directory structure for further targeted attacks. [verified: Same as finding [13]: BASE_EXPORT_DIR path in RuntimeError exception message at line 97-103; filesystem disclosure.]

Filesystem path disclosure in error messages — Internal filesystem path leaked to attacker — aids in path traversal and other file-based attack reconnaissance. [verified: RuntimeError at line 103 includes BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path in the exception message returned to client; leaks internal directory structure.]

Disabled XSS Protection and Cleared Content-Security-Policy Header — Browser XSS auditor disabled; CSP policy removed, making XSS attacks easier to exploit. [verified: Same as finding [10]: X-XSS-Protection disabled and CSP cleared at lines 141-168.]

Security headers disabled (X-XSS-Protection + CSP stripped) in case_frame_slip_424 — Disabled browser XSS auditor and removed Content Security Policy weaken defense-in-depth, making XSS exploitation easier if another injection point exists. [verified: Same as finding [10]: X-XSS-Protection='0' and CSP='' at lines 148-168; browser defense-in-depth removed.]

Configuration and Environment Variable Exposure in Response — Reconnaissance; attacker learns Django settings module path and filesystem structure. [verified: Same as finding [12]: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_EXPORT_DIR exposed in JSON response at line 153-184.]

Active disabling of X-XSS-Protection and CSP headers in /ops/frame/case-slip-424/ — Reduced browser-side protection against XSS and content injection attacks, making exploitation of other XSS vulnerabilities easier. [verified: Same as finding [10]: X-XSS-Protection='0' and CSP='' at lines 158-168; strips browser security headers.]

Information disclosure — settings module and filesystem path exposed in case_trace_panel_444 — Attacker learns internal application structure (Django settings module name) and server directory layout, enabling targeted attacks on configuration files and other resources. [verified: Same as finding [12]: JSON response at line 162-184 exposes DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE path and BASE_EXPORT_DIR.]

XSS protection and CSP headers intentionally disabled — Browser XSS auditor disabled and CSP removed — any XSS on pages served through this response path has no browser-side mitigations. [verified: Response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection='0' and Content-Security-Policy='' at lines 167-168; strips browser defense-in-depth that Django SecurityMiddleware otherwise provides.]

Environment variable and filesystem path disclosure in /ops/trace/case-panel-444/ — Reconnaissance information enabling more targeted attacks, including knowledge of the Django settings module name and internal directory structure. [verified: Same as finding [12]: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_EXPORT_DIR exposed at lines 175-184.]
